name: Turner Construction
legalName: Turner Construction Company (wholly-owned subsidiary of Hochtief AG; Hochtief is ~79-80% controlled by Grupo ACS)
founded: 1902 (Henry Chandlee Turner; acquired by Hochtief in 1999 for $370M)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Turner is America's largest general builder (ENR Top 400 #1 six consecutive years) converting itself into an AI-infrastructure prime at extraordinary speed — data-center revenue roughly tripled from $3.6B (2024) toward ~$9B (2025) on the way to a stated >$20B-per-year target by 2030, with data centers now ~42% of a record $48.9B backlog (Q1 2026) and €21.6B of trailing-twelve-month data-center orders per parent Hochtief. The award stack reads like the AI buildout itself: Meta Richland Parish LA (expanded to $50B / 5 GW, shared with DPR and Mortenson), Meta Lebanon IN ($10B / 1 GW), CoreWeave Lancaster PA ($6B, Turner-Wohlsen JV), and the $15B Vantage 'Stargate' campus for OpenAI/Oracle in Port Washington WI (Turner-McCarthy JV on phase 1). BACKGROUND: Founded 1902 in New York; wholly owned by Germany's Hochtief (itself ~79-80% ACS-controlled) since 1999 — Turner now generates ~68% of Hochtief group sales. 2025 revenue $29.2B (+40%, company-reported); Hochtief-basis operational PBT €921M (+62%) at a 3.6% margin, with FY2026 guidance of $1.40-1.46B. The enterprise moats are procurement and engineering, not the cranes: SourceBlue (~$1B annual product volume, 1,300+ OEM relationships, open-book long-lead procurement), Turner Engineering Group (six-to-nine-nines reliability), 'xPL Offsite' prefab, and the ~1,000-person Dornan Engineering M&E acquisition for Europe. Caveat from the sector tables: on trailing dedicated data-center revenue, BD+C's 2025 ranking still placed HITT, Holder, and DPR ahead of Turner — the forward backlog is where Turner's takeover of the category shows.
ecosystemRole: We assess Turner as the single largest procurement channel into the AI-infrastructure supply chain among US general contractors — and therefore a demand aggregator this ecosystem's equipment vendors sell through, not just alongside. Basis: SourceBlue's open-book OEM procurement model handles the long-lead electrical and mechanical packages (transformers, switchgear, generators, chillers) for a data-center order book running at €18-22B/year, and Turner's scale claims (~3 GW delivered per Blackridge, #4 globally) sit on top of a $44B+ backlog that is ~40% data centers. For power-chain vendors: Turner's preconstruction stage is where equipment gets specified and reserved — its 'identify long-lead equipment before it reaches the field' pitch is precisely the choke point the whole sector's schedules hinge on. The shared-award pattern on mega-campuses (Meta LA split three ways; Stargate WI split four ways) also reveals how hyperscalers dual-source GC capacity — no single builder, even the largest, gets an AI gigacampus alone.

productsAndServices.name: Critical Facilities / data-center construction
productsAndServices.description: Construction management and GC delivery for edge, enterprise, hyperscale, and colocation facilities. Company-referenced clients include Meta (Louisiana, Indiana, Jeffersonville), CoreWeave (Lancaster PA), Vantage (Ohio; the OpenAI/Oracle 'Stargate' Wisconsin campus), Aligned, Equinix, QTS, and NTT (Berlin, via Hochtief) — spanning ten-plus US states plus Turkey and Malaysia. Turner brands itself 'the largest data center builder'; independent sector tables (BD+C 2025) still ranked HITT/Holder/DPR ahead on trailing dedicated DC revenue, while Blackridge (May 2026) puts Turner #4 globally at ~3 GW delivered.
highlights: Data-center revenue $3.6B (2024) → ~$9B expected (2025); ~37-42% of backlog through 2025-26
Hochtief-reported Turner data-center orders: €18.1B in FY2025, €21.6B trailing-twelve-month at H1 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The scale play: no specialist matches the forward order intake, and megacampus owners (Meta, Vantage) hire Turner alongside rivals rather than instead of them.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: CM/GC and design-build contracts, frequently in JVs (Turner-Wohlsen for CoreWeave, Turner-McCarthy for Stargate WI) — a capacity-sharing pattern hyperscalers now impose.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Advanced technology projected to reach 40% of the total portfolio (company statement); Europe expansion through Dornan.

productsAndServices.name: SourceBlue (supply-chain & equipment procurement)
productsAndServices.description: Wholly-owned procurement subsidiary (ex-Turner Logistics, rebranded 2021): strategic sourcing of long-lead equipment with direct OEM relationships and open-book pricing — engaged at preconstruction to 'identify long-lead equipment, alternate products, and schedule risk before it reaches the field,' then expediting, delivery tracking, and warranty coordination.
highlights: ~$1B annual product volume; 1,300+ supplier relationships; 250+ procurement specialists; 600+ projects supported
Presented inside the Critical Facilities offer as 'Equipment Supply Chain Management'
productsAndServices.positioning: The de-risking arm that turns transformer/switchgear/generator/chiller lead times — the industry's binding constraint — into a managed service; for equipment vendors, SourceBlue is the buying desk behind a ~$20B/yr data-center order book.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with Turner projects and offered to outside clients.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Named by the President of Enterprise Services as a designated expansion vector.

productsAndServices.name: Turner Engineering Group, self-perform & offsite manufacturing
productsAndServices.description: TEG provides commissioning-grade reliability engineering for uptime environments 'measured in milliseconds (6/9s) to microseconds (9/9s)'; Turner's Sustainability + TEG bench counts 750+ credentialed staff. 'xPL Offsite' prefabrication cuts onsite data-center labor 10%+ (company claim). Self-Perform Operations, VDC, and a fabrication shop round out delivery control.
highlights: Dornan Engineering acquisition (closed early 2025): ~1,000-person Irish M&E/commissioning firm, €700M output, €1.1B backlog ~85% advanced-technology — self-perform M&E for Europe's data-center market
Turner cited '$20B of advanced technology project opportunities in Europe' as the Dornan rationale
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertical capability creep toward EPC-like control of the highest-value packages — the same direction the whole GC tier is moving as electrical/mechanical scope dominates AI-factory cost.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Integrated into CM/GC contracts; Dornan operates across Ireland/UK/Continental Europe/Nordics.
productsAndServices.roadmap: TEG and Self-Perform named strategic expansion priorities (Nov 2024 reorganization).

productsAndServices.name: Diversified building portfolio
productsAndServices.description: The non-DC base that made Turner #1 before AI: healthcare (300+ projects/year), aviation & transportation (1,200+ projects), sports (Buffalo Bills, Tennessee Titans, Cleveland Browns' $2.4B domed stadium), education, pharma/biotech, federal — plus megaprojects like the ~$10B NYC Midtown Bus Terminal replacement (JV with STV) and One Beverly Hills. ENR's #1 Green Builder 18 consecutive years (company claim); an active mass-timber practice.
highlights: H1 2025 backlog mix beyond DC: healthcare $6.6B, education $4.1B, sports $3.5B
150 projects with revenue >$100M as of Nov 2024
Operates in ~30 countries via Turner International
productsAndServices.positioning: The diversification that hedges the AI-capex cycle — the analyst-flagged 'tale of two markets' risk cuts both ways.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sports and transit megaprojects run through the late 2020s alongside the DC ramp.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Turner is executing a deliberate conversion from diversified builder to AI-infrastructure prime, using scale as the moat specialists can't match. Basis: data-center revenue tripling toward ~$9B in one year, €18-22B/yr of DC order intake per Hochtief, a stated >$20B-by-2030 DC revenue target, and an org restructure (Nov 2024) that created a president-level owner for the procurement/engineering enterprise services.

(High confidence) We assess the durable advantage is the procurement-and-engineering layer, not construction labor. Basis: SourceBlue's ~$1B/yr open-book OEM buying desk sits exactly on the industry's binding constraint (long-lead electrical gear), TEG sells nine-nines reliability engineering, and Dornan adds self-perform M&E — Turner is quietly assembling EPC-grade control of the packages that decide AI-campus schedules.

(Moderate confidence) We assess trailing sector rankings understate Turner's forward position. Basis: BD+C's 2025 table (2024 revenue) ranks HITT/Holder/DPR ahead in dedicated DC revenue, but Turner's FY2025 DC order intake (€18.1B) exceeds any specialist's annual DC revenue outright; unless award momentum breaks, Turner passes the specialists on delivered revenue by 2026-27. Collection gap: Turner does not publish MW delivered — the ~3 GW figure is Blackridge's estimate.

(Moderate confidence) We assess concentration and labor are the twin risks the growth is pricing in. Basis: data centers are ~42% of backlog with a handful of counterparties (Meta programs alone span $60B of campus value; OpenAI/Oracle-linked work adds more); ENR's own 2026 framing is a 'craft ceiling' as AI strains skilled labor, and analysts pressed Hochtief on Turner capacity limits at FY2025 results (management denied a ceiling). A pause in hyperscaler capex would hit the backlog's largest and youngest component first.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the governance/safety record is a manageable but real diligence item. Basis: the individual-level Bloomberg bid-rigging convictions (2020-21), the $23.5M UChicago scaffold-collapse settlement (2024-25), and prior site fatalities are third-party documented; none implicate current strategy, but they are the record a hyperscaler's vendor-risk process weighs against the safety-program claims.
